function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file. Returns up to 500 lines by default with line numbers.
For large files, a footer shows total lines and how to read the next section.

IMPORTANT:
- For large files, use start_line to continue reading from where you left off.
- Use max_lines to read smaller chunks if you only need a specific section.
- Always read a file BEFORE trying to edit it with edit_file.

path.description: Absolute or relative file path to read

start_line.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based, default: 1)

max_lines.description: Maximum number of lines to return (default: 500)

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file.

IMPORTANT:
- For EXISTING files, prefer edit_file instead — it's safer and only changes what you specify. write_file replaces the ENTIRE file.
- For NEW files, this is the right tool. Parent directories are created automatically.
- You must provide the complete file content — there is no append mode.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Replace a specific string in a file with new content. The old_text must match exactly (whitespace and indentation matter). Read the file first to get the exact text. If the edit fails, re-read the file once and retry with the correct text.

old_text.description: Exact text to find and replace (copy from the file)

function.name: list_directory
function.description:
List files and subdirectories at the given path. Shows one level only.

When to use:
- To see what files exist in a specific directory
- To verify a file path before reading

When NOT to use:
- To find files by name → use glob_files instead
- To search file contents → use grep_files instead
- If the project code structure was already provided in your context, you likely don't need this.

path.description: Directory path to list (default: project root)

function.name: glob_files
function.description:
Find files matching a glob pattern in a directory tree. Returns file paths with sizes, sorted by modification time (newest first).

When to use:
- To find files by name or extension (e.g. '**/*.py', 'src/**/*.ts')
- To see all files of a certain type in the project

When NOT to use:
- To search file CONTENTS → use grep_files instead
- To see a specific directory → use list_directory instead

path.description: Directory to search in (default: project root or cwd)

max_results.description: Maximum number of files to return (default: 100)

function.name: grep_files
function.description:
Search for a regex pattern across files in a directory tree.

Output modes:
- 'content' (default): matching lines as 'file:line_number: content'
- 'files_with_matches': only unique file paths that contain a match
- 'count': match count per file as 'file: N'

Features:
- Context lines: show N lines before/after each match
- Multiline: match patterns across line boundaries
- Case insensitive: ignore case when matching
- Type filter: shorthand for file type (e.g. 'py' instead of '*.py')

IMPORTANT:
- The path must be a DIRECTORY, not a file. To search within a single file, use read_file instead.
- Use 'include' for glob patterns or 'type_filter' for common extensions.
- Results are capped at max_results (default 50).

path.description: Directory to search in (default: project root). Must be a directory, not a file path.

include.description: Glob filter for files to include (e.g. '*.py', '*.{ts,tsx}')

type_filter.description: File type shorthand (e.g. 'py', 'js', 'ts', 'rust'). Alternative to include.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

output_mode.description: Output format: 'content' (matching lines, default), 'files_with_matches' (file paths only), 'count' (match count per file)

context_lines.description: Number of lines to show before AND after each match (default: 0)

before_context.description: Lines to show before each match (overrides context_lines for before)

after_context.description: Lines to show after each match (overrides context_lines for after)

multiline.description: Match pattern across line boundaries (default: false)

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Run a shell command and return its output. This is Windows. Do NOT use Unix commands (ls, cat, grep, head, wc). Use the dedicated tools instead: list_directory, read_file, grep_files, glob_files.

IMPORTANT:
- Do NOT use this for file searching — use grep_files or glob_files instead.
- Do NOT use this for reading files — use read_file instead.
- Foreground commands time out after 30 seconds. Do NOT run interactive programs.
- Use run_in_background=true for long-running processes (tests, servers, builds). This returns a PID immediately — use check_process to see output later.
- Use this for: syntax validation, pip install, git, python -c '...', pytest, etc.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for foreground commands (default 30, max 600)

run_in_background.description: Start the process in background and return immediately with a PID (default: false)

function.name: search_memories
function.description:
Search past conversation memories for specific information.

Your context already includes automatically-retrieved memories, but they're limited to the top results for the user's current message. Use this tool when:
- You need more detail about a topic than what's in your context
- The user asks about something specific from a past conversation
- You want to verify a fact before stating it
- The automatically-loaded context doesn't cover what the user is asking about

Returns full conversation content, not just summaries.

query.description: Search query — be specific (e.g. 'cat name' not 'what do you know about me')

function.name: web_search
function.description:
Search the web and return results.

When to use:
- User asks a factual question you're not confident about
- User explicitly asks you to search or look something up
- You need current information (news, docs, releases, prices)

When NOT to use:
- Questions you can answer from memory or general knowledge
- Coding questions where you already know the answer

Tips:
- Use specific, concise queries (like you'd type into Google)
- Include the year for time-sensitive queries (e.g. 'Python 3.13 release date 2025')
- If the first search doesn't help, try rephrasing before giving up

function.name: task_complete
function.description: Signal that the current task is finished. Call this tool when you have completed all the work requested. Include a summary of what you did, files you changed, and anything the user should know or test. Do NOT call this until you have actually made the changes — planning or describing what you would do is not completion.

summary.description: Summary of what you did (2-4 sentences)

files_modified.description: Comma-separated list of files created or modified

decisions_made.description: Key design decisions or trade-offs worth noting

function.name: ask_user
function.description:
Ask the user a question when you need clarification. Use this when:
- The task description is ambiguous or could be interpreted multiple ways
- You need to choose between multiple valid approaches
- Something has failed twice and you're unsure how to proceed
- The task would delete or significantly modify existing code

For multiple-choice questions, provide options as a comma-separated list.
Do not ask trivial questions — only ask when user input would change your approach.

question.description: The question to ask the user

options.description: Comma-separated list of options (e.g. 'Option A, Option B, Option C'). User can pick by number or type a custom answer.

allow_free_text.description: Allow user to type a custom answer beyond the options (default: true)
